newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: SOCCER-ALDRIDGE RETIRES FROM INTERNATIONAL SOCCER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALDRIDGE RETIRES FROM INTERNATIONAL SOCCER.

text.p: Republic of Ireland manager Mick McCarthy confirmed on Tuesday that veteran striker John Aldridge has decided to quit international football.

The 38-year-old former Liverpool player spent all of Ireland's goalless World Cup draw with Iceland on Sunday on the substitutes' bench when he was hoping to score the goal which would have equalled Frank Stapleton's all-time Republic record of 20 goals.
Now he plans to concentrate on his full-time job as Tranmere player-manager.
McCarthy said: "I'm disappointed but I can understand it." But he denied rumours that there had been a bust-up with the prolific striker.
"He's told me that being away for a week with the Irish team and then not getting a game is something he can't accept any more. It is a pity because he's been a great servant to Irish football."

Aldridge, who won 69 caps for his country, said it had been "a gut-wrenching decision for me to make because I have so many happy memories of my time with the Irish team. But my commitments now with Tranmere mean that I can no longer afford to be away with the international squad if I am not actually going to play."
"I was hoping to hang on for next year and have another shot at getting to the finals in France but that's not to be."
